note: The figures /accuracy opens with, from tools/build-accuracy-summary.js over data/model-verdicts.json, data/outlook-ledger.json, data/verification-ledger.json, data/observed-disasters.json and data/scan-ledger.json. One verdict per forecast. Rebuilt whenever either ledger changes.

answer.lead: Our weather models have published 509 forecasts in advance since 14 Oct 2026. 277 can be graded so far: 114 came true and 163 were false alarms.
points: A forecast is graded once every day of its window has a settled NASA POWER measurement (one at least 14 days old when fetched, because recent days are revised). 232 forecasts are still waiting; measurements have settled up to 3 Nov 2026.
By chance alone, with the same windows, about 42.4 of the 277 graded forecasts would have come true.
66 days crossed a model’s line at a place it was watching, with no forecast for it.

Our other 1,769 forecasts (4,416 recorded versions) were not made in advance. 1,663 restate an alert an agency had already issued and are not a test of our skill: 10 could be checked, 2 correct, 2 partly correct and 6 wrong, counted on new damage or impact reported inside the window. 105 are aftershock forecasts after an earthquake. 1 is a test case written after its period began.
61 significant disasters are on record. We forecast none of them in advance.
